controlled_fork.purpose: Opt-in passthrough of public author fields (author_id, full nickname, public profile URL) returned by platform public content APIs. creator_hash/mask_nickname outputs unchanged; no request-limit, login or anti-bypass changes.
controlled_fork.verify: git clone -b target-npl/public-account-fields https://github.com/Chailaoda/MediaCrawler-target-npl.git vendor/MediaCrawler-controlled && git -C vendor/MediaCrawler-controlled rev-parse HEAD
controlled_fork.record: Fork history retains the full upstream lineage (830 commits up to 68d9ef1) plus 2 controlled commits; fetchable from any clean machine. The controlled fork is installed into its OWN directory so the pinned upstream baseline is never overwritten, and builds never depend on a developer's local worktree (dev worktree at vendor/mediacrawler-fork is a convenience only).

runtime.note: All three entry points call resolve_vendor_env(); the Python interpreter, the imported MediaCrawler source tree and the git worktree used by the integrity check are always the SAME directory. The scheduler passes TARGET_NPL_VENDOR_DIR to child processes so they cannot pick a different dependency. Detecting the fork proves passthrough capability only - it does NOT replace manual confirmation of platform access permission, operator authorisation or login state.

compatibility.note: Collection adapters accept either commit but require a clean working tree and an existing .venv interpreter in the selected directory. Adding new commits requires updating this registry and re-reviewing adapter compatibility together; resolve_vendor_env() refuses any other commit before collection starts. Public-account tasks require the controlled fork commit and never fall back to the upstream baseline.
